forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Investment balances increased to £905.3m following receipt of £417m Integrated Settlement grant, managed with priority to security and liquidity
findings.detail: Following receipt of the full-year Integrated Settlement grant of £417m in April, investment balances increased significantly from £451.0m at year start to £905.3m at 30 June. The portfolio is well-diversified across deposit-taking institutions, local authorities, DMO and money market funds, with 79.4% held in 0-12 month terms for liquidity and only 1.7% beyond 12 months. Investment strategy prioritises security and liquidity before yield, in line with statutory guidance and approved treasury management strategy.
findings.matters: Large cash balances can create treasury management complexity and concentration risk; a lender wants to see that a council is managing significant liquidity prudently and not taking excessive risks to generate yield. This demonstrates disciplined investment approach.
findings.figures: Investment balances £905.3m at 30 June vs £451.0m at 1 April; increase of £454.3m mainly from Integrated Settlement grant receipt of £417m; portfolio: Banks £603.3m, Local Authorities £80.0m, DMO £85.0m, Money Market Funds £137.0m; 44.5% invested 9-12 months, 18.3% in 0-3 months
findings.quote: Investment balances increased from £451.0m at the start of the year to £905.3m at 30 June 2026, largely due to the receipt in April of the full year's Integrated Settlement grant funding of £417m. These balances are held across short-term deposits, on-call accounts, money market funds, the Debt Management Office and other local authorities, with investment decisions continuing to prioritise security and liquidity before yield.

findings.headline: External borrowing stable at £113.3m with 95.29% of portfolio at 10+ year maturity, locking in interest rate of 4.14%
findings.detail: No new borrowing was undertaken during Q1 and no early repayments made, leaving external borrowing unchanged at £113.3m (comprising £78.3m PWLB and £35.0m private sector borrowing) at an average rate of 4.14%. The maturity structure shows 95.29% of borrowing falls due in 10+ years, with minimal near-term refinancing risk. This long-dated profile locks in current interest costs and significantly reduces exposure to future rate movements.
findings.matters: Refinancing risk and debt maturity profile are key indicators of financial stability for a lender. A council with debt locked in at long maturity faces lower medium-term refinancing costs and interest rate risk.
findings.figures: External borrowing £113.3m at 4.14% average rate; PWLB £78.3m, private sector £35.0m; maturity: 95.29% due 10+ years, 4.41% due 2-5 years, 0.29% due under 12 months
findings.quote: At 30 June 2026, the Authority held £113.3 million of external loans, no change from the beginning of the year.

findings.headline: Additional staffing approved in-year driving £0.1m corporate overheads overspend, with full-year cost impact falling into 2027/28
findings.detail: Corporate overheads forecast shows expenditure of £41.3m against approved budget of £41.2m—a £0.1m overspend before recharges, driven by additional posts approved since budget was set. The original budget did not assume full-year cost of all posts in the establishment, only part-year impact of recruitment. The report notes that full-year impact of posts approved during the year will fall into 2027/28 and must be considered in MTFP refresh and future budget-setting.
findings.matters: Recurring cost increases directly affect a council's operating margin and future debt servicing capacity. Forward visibility of staffing cost trends is critical for multi-year financial planning and debt sustainability.
findings.figures: Corporate overheads £0.1m overspend (£41.3m forecast vs £41.2m budget); employee costs £23.267m forecast vs £23.165m budget (£0.102m increase); staffing-related pressure to continue into 2027/28
findings.quote: The quarter 1 forecast therefore reflects the expected part-year impact of recruitment taking place during the year, including additional posts approved since the budget was set. While this results in a relatively limited in-year pressure, the full-year impact of these posts will fall into 2027/28 and will need to be considered as part of the MTFP refresh.

findings.headline: Housing and Strategic Planning expenditure £9.8m below budget due to delays in project approvals and contracting
findings.detail: Housing programme is underspending by £9.8m, with expenditure forecast at £25.3m against budget of £35.1m. The primary driver is the Integrated Settlement housing allocation at £5.0m versus £21.9m budget. The report attributes this to the time required for projects to progress through development, appraisal, approval and contracting stages. However, the Brownfield Housing Fund continues performing, with 34 schemes approved and five complete.
findings.matters: Capital programme timing can indicate delivery capability constraints; persistent slippage in major housing initiatives affects a council's ability to execute its growth agenda and generate economic returns that support debt servicing capacity.
findings.figures: Housing expenditure £25.3m forecast vs £35.1m budget (£9.8m shortfall); Integrated Settlement housing £5.0m forecast vs £21.9m budget; Brownfield Housing Fund 34 schemes approved, 5 complete
findings.quote: Housing and Strategic Planning expenditure is forecast at £25.3m against a budget of £35.1m, representing a net variance of £9.8m below budget. The most significant movement relates to the Integrated Settlement housing allocation, where expenditure is forecast at £5.0m compared with an original budget of £21.9m.

findings.headline: Interest income forecast at £28.9m compared with approved budget of £6.8m, driven by higher cash balances and interest rates
findings.detail: Corporate overheads show net variance of £21.7m below budget, primarily due to interest income forecast at £28.9m against £6.8m budget—a £22.1m increase. This reflects higher than anticipated cash balances held during the year and current interest rates. The report explicitly states this additional interest income will be transferred to an earmarked reserve at year end and will not support recurring revenue expenditure, demonstrating prudent financial management.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether a council is using investment income to mask underlying budget pressures or fund recurring costs. This council is generating significant investment income but reserving it rather than relying on it for operations.
findings.figures: Interest income £28.9m forecast vs £6.8m budget; variance of £22.1m; to be transferred to earmarked interest reserve at year end
findings.quote: The overall net corporate overheads position is forecast to be £21.7m below budget, primarily due to interest income now being forecast at £28.9m compared with the approved budget of £6.8m.
